children: Operations is how Barkpark runs in the real world — Hetzner ARM64, a clean-rebuild deploy discipline, and background work that keeps the graph and search fresh.

Production is a single Hetzner ARM64 box. The Phoenix API runs under a systemd Service, fronted by Caddy for TLS and routing. Public traffic reaches Studio and the HTTP API v1 through that reverse proxy.

Deploy pulls from main, then performs a Blue Green Rebuild — the hard-won rule is to nuke the entire build directory before recompiling, never partially, then restart the systemd Service. A Migration runs against the production Postgres as part of bringing schema changes live. Skipping the restart leaves the old BEAM process serving stale code — a documented past mistake.

Long-running and deferred jobs run as an Oban Worker: re-projecting the Content Edges Table after a Mutation, rebuilding the Search Vector, and firing Webhooks for Cache Revalidation so the Web Demo sees fresh content. These workers are why a write on one surface ripples consistently to every other.
